title: Maximum Concurrent Bookings per Room
description:
A `bookings` table records room reservations with start and end timestamps. Using an **event sweep (sweep line) approach**, determine the **maximum number of overlapping (concurrent) bookings** at any point in time for each room.

**Table: bookings**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| booking_id | INT |
| room_id | INT |
| customer_name | VARCHAR |
| start_time | TIMESTAMP |
| end_time | TIMESTAMP |

Output columns: `room_id`, `max_concurrent_bookings`. Order by `room_id`.
solution_sql: WITH events AS (SELECT room_id, start_time AS event_time, 1 AS delta FROM bookings UNION ALL SELECT room_id, end_time, -1 FROM bookings), running AS (SELECT room_id, event_time, SUM(delta) OVER (PARTITION BY room_id ORDER BY event_time, delta DESC) AS concurrent_count FROM events) SELECT room_id, MAX(concurrent_count) AS max_concurrent_bookings FROM running GROUP BY room_id ORDER BY room_id

test_cases.description: Maximum concurrent bookings per room via event sweep

hints: Convert each booking into two events: a +1 event at start_time (booking begins) and a -1 event at end_time (booking ends). UNION ALL these two sets to build a single events timeline. When a start_time and end_time coincide, ORDER BY event_time, delta DESC ensures +1 events are processed before -1 events (a new booking starting exactly when one ends still overlaps).

Apply SUM(delta) OVER (PARTITION BY room_id ORDER BY event_time, delta DESC) as a running total. The running sum at each event represents the number of concurrently active bookings at that moment. MAX of this running sum gives the peak concurrency.
explanation: The sweep-line algorithm converts interval overlap detection into a sequential problem. Each booking contributes a +1 event at its start and a -1 event at its end. When these events are sorted chronologically per room, a running sum of the deltas tracks how many bookings are active at each moment. For room 1: Jack starts at 08:00 (running=1), Alice at 09:00 (2), Bob at 10:00 (3), Carol at 10:30 before Jack ends at 10:30 (4 → 3). The peak is 4. For room 2: Frank+Grace overlap at 09:30 (2), then Frank ends before Hank starts — so the peak is only 2. The ORDER BY delta DESC at ties ensures a start event (delta=+1) is counted before the simultaneous end event (delta=-1), correctly capturing the momentary peak. This algorithm is used in hotel room availability engines, cloud resource scheduling, and operating system process management.
